chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Ali ibn Muhammad al-Qasani, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Suleiman ibn Dawud, from Isa ibn Yunus, from al-Awza'i, from al-Zuhri, from Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him), regarding

a man who claimed upon a woman that he had married her with a guardian and witnesses, and the woman denied that. So the sister of this woman established the proof upon this man that he had married her with a guardian and witnesses, but they did not specify a time. So he (peace be upon him) wrote: 'The proof is the proof of the man, and the proof of the woman is not acceptable because the husband has established his right to the conjugal relations of this woman, and her sister wants the invalidation of the marriage. And it is not ratified, nor is her proof acceptable except with a time before her time, or with his entering (consummation) with her.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling when a woman denies marriage but her sister provides evidence with a man who claims he married her with witnesses?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi illustrates the Shia juristic principle of 'presumption of validity' (istishab) in marital disputes, where the husband's claim prevails unless the wife or her representative can prove the marriage was defective or non-existent. The ruling emphasizes that a woman's testimony alone is insufficient to overturn the husband's established right to conjugal relations (bush') without corroborating evidence of timing or consummation, reflecting the procedural rigor of Imami fiqh in protecting familial integrity.
